author: reek
body: The first thing this repository ever stored, and an honest account of what happened.

author: reek
body: A quire goes in -- two chapters of it, signed, content-addressed, through the same import gate the compiler's quotation gate uses. Then one chapter is edited and stored again, which is the ordinary thing anybody does to a repository within five minutes of being handed one.

author: reek
body: What works, works completely: the bytes survive, the hashes address them, the gate admits them, a forged body is refused, and BOTH editions remain retrievable forever because a content-addressed store cannot lose a version it has been given -- it does not overwrite, it accumulates.

author: reek
body: What does not work is stated here rather than hidden, because a dogfood test that only prints its successes is a colophon: a claim the artefact makes about itself with no witness but itself.

author: reek
body: The colophon in the quire we are storing can be checked, which is the joke and also the point: the book can tell you truthfully what it is. The library still cannot tell you where it is, or which one is the current one.

target: section:The Quire We Are Going To Store
author: reek
body: Two chapters, standing in for the real files. The bodies contain a PIPE, which the old encoding would have cut them in half at, and newlines, which no single-sector fact could hold.

author: reek
body: What the store hands back when you ask by name. It has no way to take a name, so it takes the kind, and the answer is whichever chapter was written last.
